result.title: Subliminal Learning Crosses Modalities
result.summary: Subliminal learning refers to a surprising phenomenon in language models wherein a prompt given to one model (e.g., preference for cats) can be subliminally distilled to another model via training on data that is ostensibly meaningless (e.g., number sequences). This paper shows that text-based subliminal learning transfers cross-modally, in particular, a topic/preference (e.g., animals) transferred through number sequences across vision-language models also changes how images are generated and represented. First, we show that a diffusion model using the student as its text encoder generates the student's animal more often than with the original model as its text encoder, but not its color or style. We then investigate the mechanism behind this phenomenon and which concepts transfer across modalities. A constant component of the student's change accounts for much of the shift of image representations toward the trait. Adding this component uniformly can change the generated animal, which depends on the whole prompt, but not concepts such as color or style, which are encoded in a single token. Finally, we introduce weight lens as an approach to identify a subliminal trait from the weights of a single trained model, and show that it identifies the trait of nearly every student, including traits that do not surface in generated images.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究文本中习得的偏好经无意义数字序列跨模态迁移到视觉语言模型，进而改变扩散模型的图像生成与图像表征，并分析恒定激活成分的作用，提出从权重中识别隐式特质的 weight lens。
AI.relevance_reason: 该工作不直接研究视觉推理，但其用恒定激活方向和权重探测定位隐式信息，可能可供核查 LVR 内部状态中的内容是否影响输出，以及用于贡献分配与监督诊断。
